auto_router.tier_distance_penalty_desc: Score penalty applied per tier-step away from the classified tier.
auto_router.pin_session: Pin a session to one deployment per model group
auto_router.pin_session_desc: Keeps a session on the same deployment within a group, so provider prompt caches stay warm. Turn off to load-balance every turn.
auto_router.pin_survives_idle: How long a pin survives idle (seconds)
auto_router.tier_score_ranges_failed: The tier score ranges could not be loaded from the proxy.
auto_router.heuristic_v2_desc: uses bundled calibrated four-tier probabilities with no API call
auto_router.llm_classifier_desc: calls a model to decide the tier (e.g. a small/fast model)
auto_router.heuristic_first_desc: scores locally, and only pays for the classifier when the score does not confidently land a cheap tier
auto_router.hybrid_desc: keeps the local score at any tier, and only pays for the classifier when that score lands near a tier boundary
auto_router.decide_locally_desc: A request the scorer places at or below this tier routes there without a classifier call. Anything the scorer places higher, and anything it found no signal for at all, goes to the classifier instead
auto_router.holding_tier_desc: Holding the tier keeps an agent on one model for a whole tool loop and cuts scoring cost. A turn the router cannot match to a held decision, such as one with no session id or an expired one, is scored again
auto_router.classifier_timeout_desc: How long the classifier call has before it fails and the fallback below takes over.
auto_router.classifier_fallback_desc: Applies when the classifier call errors, times out, or returns an unparseable response.
auto_router.context_budget_desc: Total characters of prior conversation sent to the classifier. Turns are taken newest first and quoted whole while they fit, so a short conversation is never cut.
auto_router.custom_keywords_desc: Optional: Add terms to the built-in list to improve classification accuracy on the technical dimension. (e.g., udp, kafka, terraform).
auto_router.select_classifier_model: Select the model that will classify request complexity
auto_router.type_keyword_press_enter: Type a keyword and press Enter
auto_router.circuit_breaker_desc: After one classifier timeout, use the fallback immediately for every session until a recovery probe succeeds. Enabled by default.
auto_router.classifier_prompt_caution: There are always exactly four tiers, so your prompt has to sort requests into four buckets, though it is free to define what they mean. Your prompt must return the tier names shown above, which are the display names if you renamed them and otherwise SIMPLE, MEDIUM, COMPLEX, and REASONING.
auto_router.heuristic_fallback_caution: The heuristic fallback still scores complexity, so if your prompt classifies something else, set the fallback below to the default model.
auto_router.legacy_prompt_caution: This is the legacy whole-prompt mode: the tier definitions and labels are frozen into this text, so renaming a tier or changing the rubric will not update it. Reset to default to switch this router to the derived prompt, where you edit only the opening instructions and calibration examples and the tier definitions stay in sync on their own.
auto_router.use_images_desc: Send inline image data to the classifier so it can choose a tier from what the image shows.
auto_router.edit_tiers_desc: Add or remove tiers to define your own set. Every custom tier needs a definition the LLM classifier routes on, and an edited set requires the LLM classification method
auto_router.tier_definition_required: A definition is required: it is the rubric the classifier routes on for this tier
auto_router.route_plan_mode: Route plan-mode requests to a minimum tier
auto_router.multiple_models_selected: Multiple models selected: the router randomly picks among them per request (or Thompson-samples within the pool when adaptive routing is on).
auto_router.pick_fallback_tier: Pick the tier classifier failures route to
auto_router.scoring_binary_desc: Binary uses the full weight for any hit. Match count uses half for one distinct matcher and full weight for two or more.
auto_router.custom_dim_desc: Keywords match the current ask. Regex scans its first 2,048 characters and permits bounded single-character repeats up to 64. The proxy validates patterns on save.
auto_router.advanced_scoring_desc: Every knob below is optional. Left untouched, the router follows the shipped defaults, so it picks up any recalibration of them rather than staying pinned to the numbers shown here.
auto_router.could_not_load_defaults: Could not load the shipped defaults, so only values this router already overrides are shown. Saving still works, and an untouched knob keeps following the defaults.
auto_router.instructions_desc: Explain what the classifier should judge. Tier definitions are managed separately below.
auto_router.calibration_examples_desc: Show representative requests and the tier they should receive. The router adds these after its tier definitions.
auto_router.could_not_load_assembled_prompt: Could not load the assembled prompt. Your text is still saved as written.
auto_router.complexity_tier_tooltip: Map each complexity tier to one or more models. Simple queries use cheaper/faster models, complex queries use more capable models.
auto_router.default_model_desc: Used when the tier the request lands in has no model, and when the classifier fails with "Route to the default model" selected.
auto_router.fallback_tier_tooltip: Where requests route when the LLM classifier errors, times out, or returns an unparseable reply. Required for an edited tier set: the heuristic scorer cannot produce your tiers.

adaptive_routing.how_it_works_desc: It learns from how each conversation actually goes: does the user have to rephrase or correct the model, does it get stuck repeating itself, does it run out of tool calls, does the user seem satisfied. Combined with cost, this live feedback shifts future routing toward the models that are actually working well, and improves as more conversations come in. Until there's enough feedback, it defaults to the classified tier's model.
adaptive_routing.quality_cost_desc: Higher quality weight favors more capable (pricier) models; higher cost weight favors cheaper models when the bandit has feedback to act on. Recommended: 30% quality / 70% cost split.
adaptive_routing.all_tiers_desc: — router can pick across tiers, depending on the best fit for the prompt
